narrative:
The 2020 Philadelphia Phillies entered the pandemic-shortened 60-game season with genuine playoff aspirations, armed with Bryce Harper's star power, J.T. Realmuto's elite catching, and a lineup built to compete in the NL East. But the condensed schedule offered no margin for error, and Philadelphia discovered that painful truth almost immediately, stumbling out of July at 1-2 before finding their footing in August.

August became the Phillies' best month and their most emotionally whiplashing stretch. Didi Gregorius delivered a stunning line drive to center field on August 11th that plated two runs and swung the game by nearly half a win probability point, while J.T. Realmuto's three-run blast on the 14th embodied the team's explosive ceiling. Scott Kingery added a dramatic three-run home run on August 28th that reminded fans what this offense was capable of. Yet for every surge, the bullpen — particularly a struggling Brandon Workman — gave it right back, and the Héctor Neris implosion on August 14th symbolized the fragility lurking beneath the surface. Still, the Phillies finished August 14-13, proving they could win even when the moments cut against them.

September was where the season unraveled. David Phelps surrendered a devastating three-run home run to Jeff McNeil on September 7th that swung the win probability by over half a point, and though Jean Segura and the electric rookie Alec Bohm — whose walk-off single on September 8th was the season's single biggest positive play — offered brief reasons to believe, the Phillies simply could not hold leads. Brandon Workman's name appeared repeatedly in the season's most damaging moments, and a Yadiel Hernandez home run on September 22nd that shifted win probability by an astonishing 0.705 was a gut-punch summary of September's futility. The team went 13-17 in the final month.

Philadelphia finished 28-32, missing the expanded 2020 playoffs and leaving a fanbase that had hoped this roster would finally break through deeply disappointed. The pieces were there — Harper flashed brilliance, Bohm arrived like a promise, and the lineup generated runs at a solid clip — but a 5.14 ERA and a bullpen that consistently squandered high-leverage moments defined a season of what-ifs. The 2020 Phillies were a team good enough to dream but not disciplined enough to deliver.

chapters.title: Early Turbulence
chapters.description: The Phillies stumble in July and open August on shaky footing, absorbing a painful Ronald Acuña home run that sets the tone for a season of bullpen vulnerability.

chapters.title: August Surge
chapters.description: Harper, Gregorius, Realmuto, and Kingery all deliver massive moments as Philadelphia goes 14-13 in August and proves the offense is capable of carrying this team.

chapters.title: Cracks in the Foundation
chapters.description: Brandon Workman's repeated late-game implosions and a brutal double-header against Miami expose the bullpen's fatal flaws just as September begins.

chapters.title: Bohm's Arrival and a Glimmer of Hope
chapters.description: Rookie Alec Bohm delivers the season's single most impactful positive play with a walk-off single, and Jean Segura's clutch homer gives fans one last moment to believe.

chapters.title: September Collapse
chapters.description: A 13-17 September finish, punctuated by crushing bullpen losses and a season-ending Yadiel Hernandez home run, ends Philadelphia's playoff hopes and defines the Phillies' 2020 ceiling.
